Lead strategy and execution of accelerated and real time aging studies including bridging studies at the device component/ subassembly/ in-process material and combination product level. Lead stablishing test methodologies/ testing readiness and execution in support of critical activities such as stability studies, drug product filling process validation, combination product final assembly process validation, shipping studies, etc. Support establishment of incoming and release tests at the component and combination product level with key functional areas. Oversee design verification activities performed by external partners. Lead/ Support clinical supplies production with respect to device component and combination product testing. Maintain a high level of engagement with cross-functional team members to effectively implement and successfully execute against design verification strategies. Stay current with new device technologies, relevant worldwide regulations, standards, and effectively share this knowledge with others. Enhance our Company’s professional image and competitive advantage through publications, presentations, patents, and professional activities. Comprehensive understanding of drug product development in addition to device development expertise. Strong familiarity with regulatory landscape associated with drug delivery combination product and design verification requirements. Strong working knowledge of standards relevant to device components and combination products, including ISO 11608, ISO 11040, ISO 80369, as well as performance tests related to container closure integrity and dose accuracy, among others. Proven track record of applying analytical skills in product test method design, development, and validation. Working knowledge of analytical test method technology transfer process. Proven ability to lead teams of different skill sets and backgrounds. Strong interpersonal skills and a strategic thinker; able to influence without formal authority; ability to influence and present ideas to senior leadership. TL;DR:

We're hiring a Product Counsel to help legal move at the speed the product ships: clearing features before they go live, making privacy true inside the product, and building the AI tools that let legal scale with the business. Zero risk equals zero growth here; your job is finding the workable path that keeps us shipping.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we’re looking for

- Relevant experience: You hold a law degree and qualification in a major jurisdiction (EU member state, UK, or US), and you have 3 to 6 years of practice, including time counseling product or technology teams at or for a consumer-facing technology or SaaS company (in-house or through secondment).

- Launch judgment: You have cleared products that millions use, under real deadlines, and you can walk us through your risk calls: one thing you cleared, one you blocked, one you fixed so it could ship.

- AI and privacy fluency: You have applied GDPR inside a live product (consent, data use, deletion) and handled real AI legal questions: training data, provider terms, or transparency duties. You do not need a privacy certification; you need to have worked on real features, and you get to depth fast.

- Consumer-scale instincts: You write terms that hold against millions of users, and you handle consumer protection, content, and intermediary liability with confidence.

- Pragmatic risk tolerance: You can recommend with 70 percent of the information and say what would change your mind. Answers over memos.

- Automation first: You use AI tools daily and expect to automate the repeatable parts of your own job.

- High energy, fast to learn: Quick into domains you have never touched, unbothered when priorities change weekly.

- Location: Stockholm, in office (we support relocation). Comfortable with occasional US-hours overlap; part of the team is in San Francisco. Fluent English; Swedish is not required.

- Bonus: Platform or marketplace experience; open-source licensing depth (copyleft, patent exposure); EU regulatory range beyond privacy (DSA, e-Privacy, EEA consumer law) or the US equivalents; you don’t need to read code but you should have a growth mindset and enjoy digging into using new tech. For example, you have built something with Lovable. Include the link when you apply; it is the fastest way to stand out.

What you’ll do

- Embed with product and engineering: Review features, integrations, and launches before they ship, and give go/no-go answers calibrated to actual risk: what clears, what blocks, what ships with a fix. Recent questions on this desk: a health-data connector, AI agents that publish user apps, open-source licensing in the client, ownership of AI-generated code, marking AI-generated content.

- Handle privacy and AI issues inside the product: Data use in new features, consent and disclosure mechanics, opt-out and deletion controls that work end to end. You get into the design while it is still soft and make features match our positions.

- Own product-facing terms: Feature and beta terms, program terms (partners, freelancers), and the user-facing communications when products change or sunset, and contribute to Terms of Service changes.

- Run our AI compliance mechanics: Track EU AI Act transparency and content-marking duties, map obligations against the product roadmap, and support model provider negotiations: make sure retention caps and training bans hold up in the product, not just on paper.

- Answer consumer and platform questions at scale: Marketing claims, consumer protection across the EEA and US, user-generated content and moderation, and liability for what users build and publish through us.

- Back up commercial in enterprise deals: Own the standard answers on training, retention, IP ownership, and hosting liability, and join customer calls when it moves a deal.

- Build systems, not queues: Self-serve guidance, launch checklists, and AI agents that handle the repeatable reviews. We build our own legal tooling on Lovable, and heavy daily AI use is the default here, for lawyers too.

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

As a Law Enforcement Liaison (Kansas), you’ll develop and advance strategic law enforcement and safety relationships with special focus on law enforcement, while also supporting internal platform safety efforts that elevate the Roblox safety ecosystem. The ideal candidate will be a versatile, self-driven, team-player who enjoys context-switching across high-profile initiatives, and is uniquely motivated by Roblox’s mission of connecting a billion people with optimism and civility. From serving as an external representative of Roblox with state and local law enforcement agencies, to collaborating cross-functionally with our Legal & Advocacy, Civility, Safety, Product, and Communications teams (among others), you will have a diverse set of responsibilities in furtherance of assisting law enforcement, educating external stakeholders such as parents and educators on digital safety, and ultimately helping keep users safe on Roblox.

This position is remotely based in Kansas and will report to the Senior Manager of US Public Policy.

Please note: This role requires On-Call support during weekends and holidays, and is expected to include frequent travel. The scope may also require reviewing graphic, controversial, and offensive content in accordance with Roblox’s handling policies.

You Will:

• Develop and advance strategic law enforcement relationships with special focus on law enforcement in the State of Kansas, and Midwestern region, while assisting with global outreach as needed.
• Coordinate with federal, state, and local law enforcement, including with the Kansas Attorney General’s Office
• Plan and execute educational programs for law enforcement agencies and other key external stakeholders (i.e. parent groups and educators) regarding Roblox’s platform safety efforts, including our law enforcement response policies and NCMEC CyberTip initiatives.
• Proactively identify, monitor, analyze, and internally advise on law enforcement developments affecting Roblox in the State of Kansas and Midwestern region.
• Seek to understand and empathetically respond to regional law enforcement concerns, while helping internally codify and scale resultant learnings.
• Listen to and understand the concerns of Kansas parents, caregivers, and educators regarding the safety of Roblox. You will provide guidance and education that empower these audiences and build confidence in Roblox’s emphasis on product and policy safety, which keeps users safe and healthy.
• Forge a deep subject-matter expertise of Roblox’s internal and external safety practices, so as to identify, advocate for, and help implement strategic safety enhancements.
• Draft professional work product – for both internal and external audiences – supported by clear, concise, and multi-sourced platform safety investigations.
• Collaborate and build strong internal relationships across our Legal & Advocacy, Safety, Product, and Communications teams (among others) to help address law enforcement emergencies, platform safety escalations, and comprehensive Roblox undertakings.

You Have:

• 10+ years of work experience in law enforcement, intelligence, government, trust and safety, or an adjacent field.
• Detailed knowledge of the law enforcement community and related policymakers in the State of Kansas, and Midwestern region, along with current trends and challenges in online safety and policy (particularly child safety and regional-specific considerations).
• Enthusiasm for and a demonstrated track record of stellar public speaking, short-notice travel, building and maintaining constructive relationships, defining your own work processes, and adding organizational value no matter how small or large the task.
• Outstanding communication, leadership, and stakeholder management skills.
• Agility to navigate ambiguity, resilience to overcome obstacles, and the internal drive to concurrently manage multiple high-profile, time-sensitive initiatives in a dynamic environment.
• Unwavering integrity, collegiality, and grit.

jobs.description: Work Schedule Standard (Mon-Fri) Environmental Conditions Office Job Description Role Purpose The OEM Computer Specialist is the technical visionary responsible for the "compute backbone" of Thermo Fisher’s instrumentation portfolio. This role bridges the gap between scientific instrument design and the rapid release cycles of Tier-1 hardware (Dell, HP), silicon (NVIDIA, Intel), and software (Microsoft) partners. Key Responsibilities 1. Enterprise Harmonization & Governance Multi-Divisional Standards: Drive the harmonization of computer and OS architectures across disparate Thermo Fisher divisions (Analytical Instruments, Life Sciences, Specialty Diagnostics) to leverage enterprise-scale buying power and simplify global support. Strategic Interface Management: Negotiate requirements between Thermo Fisher’s specialized scientific groups , Tier-1 hardware vendors (Dell/HP), and external integrators to ensure a consistent, branded, and high-performance product. Lifecycle Convergence: Harmonize mismatched product lifecycles across the enterprise by coordinating "Last Time Buy" programs and multi-year supply strategies for shared hardware components. Compliance Unification: Consolidate to a single quality management framework for computer systems validation (CSV), reducing redundant documentation efforts across divisions while maintaining rigorous FDA 21 CFR Part 11 standards. Design Synchronization: Help create a unified framework for "Golden Images" and hardware builds that allows different instrument groups to share core components while maintaining the ability to specialize where scientifically necessary. 2. Strategic Lifecycle & Roadmap Management Multi-Tier Lifecycle Alignment: Synchronize the 10-year lifecycle of scientific instruments with the 18–36 month refresh cycles of Tier-1 vendors. Secure "Extended Lifecycle" (XE/XL) hardware to prevent premature obsolescence. Supplier Diplomacy: Act as the primary technical interface for Dell OEM Solutions, NVIDIA, and Microsoft, influencing their future roadmaps to meet the specific power, thermal, and stability needs of lab environments 3. Regulatory Compliance & Validation Define Validated Base Images: Architect and maintain "Locked Configurations" for OS and hardware (e.g., Windows 10/11 IoT Enterprise LTSC) to ensure a stable, reproducible environment required for Installation (IQ) and Operational Qualification (OQ) , FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and GxP compliance. Serviceable Security: Negotiate cybersecurity requirements to protect instruments from network threats while ensuring the OS is not so "locked down" that Field Service Engineers (FSEs) cannot perform diagnostics or local repairs. Quality Risk Management: Conduct Validation Risk Assessments (RA) for any proposed computer hardware changes, ensuring that technology refreshes do not compromise the instrument’s validated state. 4. Integrator & Operations Management Integrator Governance: Direct third-party Computer Integrators (e.g., Unicom, Avnet, MBX) on custom hardware builds, including custom BIOS settings, branding/labeling, and specialized shock-resistant packaging. Integrator Management: Act as the primary technical point of contact for external Computer Integrators. Oversee the conversion of standard Tier-1 (Dell/HP) hardware into "Thermo Fisher Branded" appliances through custom imaging, BIOS configuration, and hardware hardening. Custom Hardware Engineering: Specify and validate mechanical customizations, including custom labeling (branding/regulatory silk-screening), specialized packaging (shock-vibration protection), and unique physical security features (port blockers, custom cabling). OS & Image Governance: Manage the delivery and maintenance of golden images (Windows LTSC/Linux) to the integrator. Ensure the deployment of "Locked" OS environments that disable non-essential services to guarantee instrument stability and security. Supply Chain Continuity: Manage "Long-Term Stocking" programs and "Last-Time-Buy" (LTB) events with the integrator to bridge gaps between Dell/NVIDIA hardware EOL dates and the end-of-support dates for Thermo Fisher instruments. Required Qualifications Education: B.S. or greater in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Experience: 3+ years in systems architecture, specifically within an OEM integration or industrial computing context Technical Expertise: Deep understanding of computer hardware fundamentals (CPU, RAM, data logic).Strong knowledge of Dell/HP OEM portfolios and NVIDIA GPU architectures . Expertise in Windows IoT Enterprise LTSC and Linux hardening. Soft Skills: Exceptional strategic thinking, analytical problem-solving, and the ability to articulate complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences. Enterprise Architecture: Strong understanding of Enterprise Architecture (EA) governance principles and their application in industrial/scientific environments. Technical Soft Skills: Demonstrated ability to negotiate technical requirements across competing internal departments (Quality, Cybersecurity, Engineering, and Field Service). Cybersecurity Knowledge: Familiarity with Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools and their impact on high-performance computing environments. Manufacturing Instruction & SOPs: Develop the detailed "Build-to-Order" (BTO) documentation for the integrator, defining everything from drive partitioning to the exact torque specs for custom mounting brackets. Quality Audit Participation: Participate in technical audits of the integrator’s facilities to ensure their production lines meet the quality standards required for medical device and life science instrumentation. Preferred Qualifications Service Background: (Preferred) Prior experience in field service or technical support to provide "empathy-driven design" for the serviceability of the system. Leadership Presence: Proven ability to influence and lead cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders in a highly matrixed global organization. Conflict Resolution: Act as the final arbiter when "Security Requirements" conflict with "Instrument Performance" (e.g., anti-virus scans interrupting high-speed data acquisition from a mass spec).
